newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt track falling U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt track falling U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Emerging market debts took a dive with the U.S. Treasuries after the closely watched March non-farm payrolls report showed strong gains in average hourly wages which could lead to wage-driven inflation, traders and analysts said.
Spreads of emerging debts over Treasuries were mostly wider. Spreads of various Brazil papers, however, were mixed, outperforming the general market, they said.
While there was some fresh selling from investors, most of the activities were among dealers, said a trader with a U.S. investment bank.
So far the outflow from emerging market funds had been moderate, compared to the exodus during previous periods when rising U.S. rates threatened liquidity, he said.
While par bonds took a heavy hit, discounts also suffered steep losses especially among the lower-grade, high yield papers, traders said.
The upgrade of Argentina and Brazil by Standard and Poor's might have lent some support to Brazil, but Argentina debt prices dropped in line with the general market, they said.

Except for the fixed rate C bond, Brazil papers tended to be lower yield floaters, which were less sensitive to rising U.S. rates, said Luis Luis, emerging market debt analyst at Scudder Stevens and Clark.
A large domestic investors base in Brazil also made the debt papers more liquid, he said.
In contrast, the Argentine market is more vulnerable to U.S. rates due to the currency peg connection, Luis said.
But once the market gets over its current "technical" phase, the fundamental strengths that drove the upgrade would come into play, he said.
Brazil C was off 3/8 at 74-5/8, while Argentina FRBs fell 1/4 at 89-3/8.
Argentina Republic 17, which has rapidly taken over FRB as a bellwether issue, dropped 1/2 to 102.00 bid.
Traders noted that the turnover of sovereign eurobonds was brisk, as some dealers and brokers used offsetting positions in eurobonds to hedge their Brady exposures.
The burgeoning repo market in emerging market eurobonds also brought more liquidity to the market and enabled players to take long and short positions, they said.
Mexico UMS 26 underperformed Bradys due to its long duration, traders said. The issue was off 5/8 to bid 102-1/4.
Like Latin debts, East European and Russian debt papers also came under the spell of U.S. Treasuries.
Bulgaria IAB fell 1/2 to 57-1/4 bid and Russia dollar Vnesh slipped 3/8 to 76-3/4 bid.
